idea: tiny CLI that prints the current moon phase, with a fun ascii moon
spec_digest: improvement run on shipped v0.1.0 moon CLI: harden tests, close known-issues, polish docs for truth - NO new features, no new runtime deps, core astronomy not rewritten
must: KI-1 closed with evidence, KI-6 fixed (consistent throw), KI-7 bounded by a declared+SAMPLED supported domain, KI-5 pinned by a measuring test
every added test closes a NAMED untested surface; test count is not an outcome
non-goals: no new flags/features, no npm publish, no dependencies, no emoji/color
taste: the risk is CHURN - one test pinning a real defect beats ten restating a pass

decisions.what: port a documented Meeus/Duffett-Smith algorithm into zero-dep Node rather than fork prior art
decisions.why: prior-art scout returned stance `extend` — the phoon lineage (Poskanzer -> moontool -> wwn-phoon-rs) is grep-verified to do real phase math offline, so re-deriving the core would be wasted work. But the cleanest candidate is Rust, which conflicts with the user's explicit node/npx/zero-install choice — and npx distribution is itself one of the three things NO prior art does. Resolution: honor `extend` in substance by porting a published algorithm and using tidecal (MIT, Meeus ch.47 in JS) as reference and wwn-phoon-rs as a cross-check oracle, while keeping the Node surface.

decisions.what: hemisphere inferred from system IANA timezone via a static table, with --south/--north override
decisions.why: hemisphere-correct art is the single differentiator verified absent in ALL prior art (moontool mirrors only its emoji; wwn-phoon-rs has zero hemisphere code). Intl exposes the TZ name offline, satisfying the no-network non-goal. Equator-straddling zones will be wrong, which is exactly what the explicit override exists for.

decisions.what: all three nice-to-haves (next-phase countdown, --date, moon age) CUT at lock
decisions.why: taste judge scored scope-fits-night 6 against the 90-minute clock and warned the accuracy claim is the thing most likely to silently slip to 'mean formula plus a few terms'. Since the entire pitch is that a wrong answer is worse than no answer, the periodic corrections must not compete for clock with optional features.

decisions.what: test_cmd set to `node --test test/*.test.js`, not `node --test test/`
decisions.why: prior run (aphorism-cli, same host, Node 24) recorded that the directory form fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Adopting the known-good form at kickoff instead of rediscovering it mid-run.

decisions.what: improvement run scoped to known-issue closure + named-surface test hardening + doc truth; the original build spec is preserved (tag v0.1.0) and remains binding, this SPEC only scopes what may change
decisions.why: allocator auto-kickoff under TRICKLE posture (allow_premium_pct 0, opus_used_pct 95) with brief 'harden tests, fix playbook items, polish docs - no new features'. The stress-test's landing attack was that housekeeping's toy version is CHURN - reworded prose plus duplicate tests. The named-surface rule is the structural answer: a test that cannot name the surface it closes does not get written.

decisions.what: KI-5 (glyph East Asian Width) stays DEFERRED as a fix, but gets pinned by a measuring test this run
decisions.why: the honest fix is a glyph-set redesign (L-effort, rewrites the product's visual core). Dispatching that under gear-1 crawl with premium at 95 pct consumed is the wrong spend. Pinning the measured widths in a test converts a prose-only caveat into a machine-checked one at S-effort - the defect can no longer drift silently.

decisions.what: astronomia v4.2.0 (MIT, a genuine Meeus port in JS) found by the scout and deliberately NOT adopted as a cross-check oracle
decisions.why: zero runtime dependencies is a must-have of the original spec. Even as a devDependency it would weaken the zero-dep story for a convenience the existing hand-computed Meeus 49.a/49.b fixtures already provide.

decisions.what: T-102 and T-103 routed to sonnet, NOT flagged route_class:'core' despite playbook L-026 (route the correctness core to fable)
decisions.why: both touch src/astro.js, but neither changes the Meeus math: T-102 adds a guard clause on a return value and T-103 adds a declared constant plus a sampled test whose domain the conductor already measured. L-026 earned its keep on items requiring astronomy judgement; spending fable here under trickle posture (allow_premium_pct=0, opus_used_pct=95) would buy nothing. Recorded so the retro can check whether this call held.

decisions.what: a ladder escalation earned by a FAILED gate outranks the gear-1 demotion rule; T-101 retries at sonnet and must not be demoted back to haiku
decisions.why: the two rules collide on docs items: the routing ladder escalates haiku->sonnet after a failed attempt, while gear-1 demotion pushes docs items sonnet->haiku. Applying them in sequence returns the item to the exact tier that just produced a fabricated number, which would reproduce the defect and burn a second cycle for nothing. Escalation is a response to observed evidence about THIS item; demotion is a budget posture. Evidence wins. Recorded for the retro as a candidate playbook lesson.

decisions.what: docs items on this run get a no-unsourced-numbers gate check as a standing rule, not just for T-101
decisions.why: the improvement run's whole premise is doc truth, and the cycle-2 failure was a plausible-sounding quantity invented to make a sentence read better. A qualitative structural claim ('zero periodic corrections vs a full Meeus series') is verifiable from the repo; a magnitude is not unless it is computed in-repo and shown. Every remaining docs item (T-101 retry, T-108) is gated on this.

decisions.what: T-102 (KI-6 fix) built this cycle instead of the priority-1 T-101 docs retry
decisions.why: both are H-value S-effort must-haves, so backlog priority does not settle it and cycle.md step 4 makes value scoring the authority. The tiebreak was gate objectivity after a no-value cycle: T-102's acceptance is checkable by running the module (it throws or it does not), whereas T-101's is source-tracing prose - the same class of check that just failed. At k=1 under gear-1 crawl a cycle buys exactly one item, so it should buy the one most likely to convert to verified value. T-101 stays priority 1 and is next; its attempts counter is untouched by this deferral.

decisions.what: the cycle-2 gate's STATED reason for failing T-101 is corrected in the record: the ~4-hour figure DOES exist in-repo (README.md:156-157, REPORT.md:34, test/astro.test.js:96). The gate DECISION is upheld unchanged.
decisions.why: cycle 2 recorded 'the string 4-hour appears NOWHERE in the repo', which was a grep for the hyphenated literal only; the repo carries it in words. Leaving that in the record would have been a false premise sitting in the retro and in the item notes, and worse, a builder retrying the item would grep, find the number, and reasonably conclude the prohibition was mistaken. The real defect is narrower and survives the correction: the figure is one hand-computed datapoint for the 2000-01-06 lunation, shown with its work in README's Accuracy section, and attempt 1 lifted it into a general per-package error claim about lunarphase-js - a package nobody ran. Unsupported generalization, understating besides (largest single ch.49 periodic term ~0.40720 d ~= 9.8 h, and the terms sum). The retry brief was written WITH the correction in it, which is why attempt 2 introduced no magnitude at all instead of arguing with a premise it could disprove.

decisions.what: the no-unsourced-numbers docs gate is restated as a frame rule, not an existence rule: a quantity may appear only in the frame in which the repo already computes it
decisions.why: the cycle-2 wording ('do not quantify unless the number is computed in-repo and shown') passes attempt 1's fabrication only because that exact string was absent. It would NOT have caught the same defect written as 'nearly four hours off' - a phrasing the repo does contain, in a different frame. The frame rule catches both: a single-lunation comparison may not be re-used as a general per-package bound. Applied to T-108, which inherits the last docs work of the run.

decisions.what: T-104 (priority 4) built ahead of T-103 (priority 3, H-value) because gear 1 makes T-103 INELIGIBLE, not merely lower-value
decisions.why: Gear 1's work-choice rule allows haiku-priced work plus S-effort sonnet builds only, and T-103 is M-effort. This is a different reason from cycle 3's T-102-over-T-101 call, which was a value tiebreak between two eligible items - recording the distinction so the retro does not read a posture constraint as a judgement about T-103's worth. T-103 remains the top must-have and should be the first pick in any cycle that clears gear 1; its attempts counter is untouched. The rule also had a real cost worth naming: KI-7, a named must-have, is now waiting on a budget posture rather than on anything about the work.

decisions.what: T-104 stayed at sonnet under a gear that demotes; a test-authoring item is build-class, not docs/polish
decisions.why: Gear 1 sets demote=true, which drops non-judgment items one rung - but its sonnet->haiku step is explicitly scoped to docs/polish items, and build/fix never drops below sonnet. An item whose output is executable test code is build-class work: the cycle-2 failure showed what happens when a tier that cannot check itself is handed work whose defects are invisible to a reader. Consistent with gear 1's own 'S-effort sonnet builds only' allowance, which would be incoherent if the demotion rule then pushed those same builds to haiku.

decisions.what: T-103 (M-effort, the run's last open must-have) SPLIT into T-103a (module constant + sampled test, S) and T-103b (README sentence, S, deps on T-103a). T-103a built and verified this cycle.
decisions.why: Gear 1 allows S-effort sonnet builds only, so T-103 had been ineligible for two consecutive cycles (recorded at cycle 5) while being the only remaining must-have. Rather than let a named must-have wait on a budget posture I do not control, I decomposed it at the file boundary. The split is not a workaround dressed up as a plan: it is the better decomposition. The original ordering would have put a domain figure into README in the same item that established it, and the standing docs frame rule (cycles 2 and 4) says a quantity may appear only in the frame the repo already computes it in. Splitting with the TEST first means the README sentence in T-103b is sourced to a shipping assertion by construction rather than by a reviewer remembering to check. The split also costs nothing if the posture lifts: at gear 2+ the two slices simply run as one k=2 wave.

decisions.what: CORRECTION to the record: runfile budget.weekly.ceiling has been carrying 1 since cycle 0, which is not a value bin/swarm-budget.sh can emit. Gear 1 rests on the ALLOCATOR posture, not on the weekly governor. Gear is unchanged at 1; only the stated reason is corrected.
decisions.why: Read the script directly this cycle (reading is permitted; hard rule 5 fences writes, not reads). Its ceiling ladder is WCEIL in {5,3,2}: weekly_heat above 1.3 gives ceiling 2 plus a promote block; above 1.1 gives ceiling 3; otherwise 5. opus_heat above 1.2 sets promote_blocked ONLY, never a ceiling. Current weekly_heat = 67.0/64.38 = 1.04, below 1.1, so the script would emit ceiling 5 with promote_blocked true from opus_heat 1.49. Prior cycles conflated the allocator posture with the weekly governor and wrote a ceiling the tool has no way to produce. The gear itself is still correct at 1 (allocator posture trickle, allow_overall_pct 0, allow_premium_pct 0, dial 0.30, unchanged for six cycles), but the STATED reason was wrong, and a wrong reason in the record is what makes a later cycle reason wrongly. It matters materially: a governor ceiling would be fixed for the run, whereas an allocator posture is refreshed by the pacer and can lift. That is the difference between the claim that T-103 is permanently ineligible and the claim that it is ineligible until the posture changes. Only the second is true, and I had drafted the first before checking.

decisions.what: T-103b FAILED the gate on one clause ('confirmed by test/astro.test.js') and was reverted rather than conductor-patched, even though the repair is a single word and this is the run's last open must-have
decisions.why: Three rules pointed the same way and the cheap path violated all three. cycle.md step 6.4 is unconditional - fail means todo + attempts+1, and it does not carve out small fixes. Step 6.5 forbids opening a gate by weakening it; a conductor editing the artifact so its own gate passes is that failure mode even when the edit is honest, because nothing independent then checks the conductor's wording. And cycle 2 established on this very run that escalation is the response to observed evidence about an item - a rule that only binds when it is inexpensive is not a rule. The cost is real and named: one more k=1 cycle spent on a one-clause repair, with the run's last must-have still open. It is affordable - 22.0 h remain to stop_at - and the alternative buys a closed must-have at the price of the only mechanism keeping doc claims honest.

decisions.what: the gate's decisive check was a HEDGE-PARITY comparison against the module and test, not a reading of the prose
decisions.why: 'Confirmed' vs 'sampled' is exactly the kind of judgement that dissolves into taste if argued as wording, and I would have been arguing it against an agent self-report that explicitly claimed 'frame rule respected'. Mechanising it settled it: extract the hedge vocabulary actually present in src/astro.js's doc comment ('sampl', 'not proven', 'no contradiction', 'stride') and in test/astro.test.js (comment line 386 'This SAMPLES -- never exhaustively sweeps --', test name ending '(sampled)'), then check whether ANY of it survived into the added README text. None did, and 'confirmed' appeared instead. That makes the finding reproducible by anyone, and it produced the falsifiability discriminator that justifies the fail: if the implementation were wrong at an unsampled instant inside the domain, the module comment stays true and the README sentence becomes false. Generalisable beyond this item - a docs claim may be checked against the hedge vocabulary of the code it documents.

decisions.what: wave autotune read this as the REVERTED branch, not as 'any other outcome': k_current 4 -> 3, wave_streak 0
decisions.why: At k=1 the run dispatches into the working tree rather than a branch (recorded cycle 6), so a failed gate reverts with `git checkout` - cycle 6 recorded that this gives the same guarantee as dropping a branch, and the equivalence has to hold in both directions or it is just a convenience. One failed verify out of one item dispatched is a 100% failure rate for the wave. Also corrects an overhang cycle 6 flagged against itself: k_current had climbed to 4 on two clean k=1 waves, ahead of anything this run has actually exercised, while the gear cap of 1 is what binds. No practical effect this cycle - min(3, gear cap 1) is still 1.

known_issues.desc: settings.json allowlist edit denied AGAIN at the improvement-run kickoff 2026-08-14 (recurring, same as the original run). permissions.additionalDirectories is still [] and bin/swarm-budget.sh + bin/swarm-playbook.sh are not allowlisted, so the budget probe and playbook parser are both unrunnable from a headless conductor and were worked around (allocator.json for gear evidence; direct file read for the playbook). Headless relaunches must keep passing --add-dir explicitly. SWARM-side tooling gap, not a target defect - hard rule 5 forbids fixing it from inside a run.
terminal font/width variance for the Unicode glyphs is an untested surface (taste judge, product-not-demo axis). No automated check can cover it; requires a human look.

Disc glyphs span two East Asian Width classes (U+2591 and U+2590 are Neutral; U+2592/3/2588/258C/258F/2595 are Ambiguous). In terminals that render ambiguous-width as double (CJK locales, iTerm2 ambiguous-as-double, xterm -cjk_width) the disc is 5-9 columns instead of 5: the single line jitters between nights, the two-line form stops aligning, and the --block frame does not close. Verified by measurement. Not a typo but an upstream Unicode fact - no Block Elements subset gives a 4-step ramp plus a symmetric half-block pair in one width class. Correct in default Western-locale terminals. Documented in README; fix needs a glyph-set redesign, deliberately deferred rather than rushed at the buzzer. MACHINE-PINNED at cycle 5 (T-104): test/render.test.js derives the disc's glyph alphabet from actual renderLine/renderBlock output and asserts it against the documented partition, so the defect can no longer drift silently - the fix (glyph-set redesign) remains deliberately deferred. The pin also EXPOSED a scope gap in the README's glyph list: the disc additionally draws U+25D6/U+25D7 (round limb), which the width caveat never mentions. Tracked as T-109.

At absurd epochs (+/-270,000 years) phaseName and illumination can contradict each other, because phaseName derives from the ch.49 instant tables and illumination from the ch.48 elongation series, and the two polynomials diverge. Zero contradictions across 350,592 states sampled over 2020-2040. Noted so it is not rediscovered as a live bug. BOUNDED (module half) at cycle 6 by T-103a: src/astro.js exports PHASE_ILLUMINATION_CONSISTENCY_DOMAIN declaring years 1000-3000, and test/astro.test.js samples 4000 deterministic points across it asserting the phase-name band discriminator (new below 0.10, crescents below 0.5, gibbous above 0.5, full above 0.90; quarters straddle and are exempt). Conductor-verified non-vacuous (3733 of 4000 samples reach a real assertion, all four bands exercised) and failable (widening the constant to year 80000 turns it red at +045200-07-01, proving the test reads the constant rather than a re-typed literal). Independently re-sampled at N=9973 and N=50021 on a jittered off-lattice: 0 violations. The bound is SAMPLED-clean, not proven, and is DECLARATIVE ONLY - nothing enforces it at runtime, deliberately, since a runtime guard is a behavior change the run's non-goals forbid. The README half is T-103b; the must-have cannot be checked off until it lands.

resolved_issues.desc: nextFullMoon() returned an Invalid Date past the top of the JS Date range instead of throwing, so --json would surface it as an uncaught RangeError from toISOString().
resolved_issues.evidence: src/astro.js:326-329 guards the constructed result with Number.isNaN(...getTime()) and throws TypeError, matching the module's existing bad-input guard. Conductor-run: nextFullMoon(new Date(8.64e15)) -> TypeError (same constructor as the bad-input throw), no RangeError escapes the toISOString path, and the guard does not over-trigger (year 1000-3000 probes + live clock all return valid strictly-later Dates). Boundary located by 60-step bisection at input +275760-09-07T01:05:02.396Z. Non-vacuity: the pinning test FAILS against `git show HEAD:src/astro.js`.
